cases.customer_question: How should inter-layer consistency errors be resolved when combining multiple Bluetooth qualification references in a Multi-Design declaration?
question_variants: Why does my Multi-Design declaration fail consistency checks?
How do I resolve LL and RF PHY ICS mismatches?
What should I do when AoA/AoD features cause declaration inconsistencies?
Can I edit the LL ICS to eliminate qualification conflicts?
When is a subset design required for Multi-Design qualification?
cases.actual_issue: Combining multiple qualification references created LL-to-RF PHY consistency-check failures involving AoA, AoD, and Isochronous capability declarations.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The selected qualification references did not declare the same Bluetooth capabilities, causing qualification-system consistency errors. Although manually changing the ICS appears possible, doing so would trigger extensive new testing obligations. The preferred solution is to obtain a subset qualification design from the original qualification owner that already removes the unsupported features.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant identified multiple inter-layer inconsistencies between included qualification references, specifically involving AoA, AoD, and Isochronous functionality. Directly modifying the LL ICS would create extensive Link Layer testing requirements. Instead, the consultant recommended obtaining a subset design from the qualification owner with the affected LL ICS items changed from supported to unsupported. The customer later confirmed that Silicon Labs provided alternative qualification references that eliminated the inconsistency.
cases.decision_logic: Qualification references must remain internally consistent across protocol layers. When included designs expose unsupported features, a qualification-owner-generated subset design preserves consistency without triggering new testing obligations.
cases.final_recommendation: Use an approved subset design or alternative qualification reference from the original listing owner that aligns capability declarations across all included layers before completing the Multi-Design declaration.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Editing the LL ICS directly can generate hundreds of additional Link Layer test requirements and significantly increase qualification effort. Unresolved consistency-check failures can prevent successful product registration.
